Messages.Author: Christian Kraus
Messages.Body:
Our group has recently been discussing the Chainsaw. The general
consensus is that as it stands it is a useless weapon when compared to
the shotgun.

What I would like to see from the Jyhad community, is some discussion on
the physics of wielding a chainsaw in combat and whether increased strength
equates to increased damage when using it.

A question for people also. Do players think that it isn't a melee weapon
because of

a) an oversight by WotC
b) play balance decision - If chainsaw is melee, why not Talbot's also.
Ugh! 3 dmg melee weapon is very good.
c) Realism (from WotC, nahh!)

I realise from the House Rulings list, that there is already support for
the Chainsaw to become a melee weapon, but I'd like to know why.

Messages.Author: L. Scott Johnson
Messages.Body:
ckr...@shell02.ozemail.com.au (Christian Kraus) writes:

>Our group has recently been discussing the Chainsaw. The general
>consensus is that as it stands it is a useless weapon when compared to
>the shotgun.

>What I would like to see from the Jyhad community, is some discussion on

>the physics of wielding a chainsaw in combat and whether increased strength
>equates to increased damage when using it.

>A question for people also. Do players think that it isn't a melee weapon
>because of
>
> a) an oversight by WotC
> b) play balance decision - If chainsaw is melee, why not Talbot's also.
> Ugh! 3 dmg melee weapon is very good.
> c) Realism (from WotC, nahh!)

It's probably not a melee weapon due to the fact that it is a chainsaw -
and will be doing large damage regardless of weilder's strength.

Oversight by WotC - only in editting. It probably should've had card
text 'Only usable once per round' instead of 'Once per Combat'. It's
easy to image how the two got confused - esp. since the Shotgun has the
'Once per Combat' text already - and WotC editors are Cut-n-Paste-happy.

Why would a chainsaw only be usable once per combat?
Does it automatically choke when you swing it? I don't think so.
A Shotgun? sure - you have to reload, and combat is too quick for reloading.

Once per round, if it was the intention, was probably more for game balance
than for any concern for realism. Although the case can be made that a
chainsaw isn't balanced for combat, so you have to work harder to control
it - which might be enough to preclude additional strikes in a round.

(Talbot's chainsaw, perhaps, is "magically animated" or somesuch, so as to
avoid such restriction :-).

----
The tendency to "fix" the chainsaw and make it a melee weapon is probably
due to the ease and obviousness of that fix. Once per Round is (IMHO) a
better, more realistic fix that fits better with the card text and TC.

Messages.Author: Johan Meijdam
Messages.Body:
Alan Kwan wrote:
> I don't really see why a Chainsaw that can be used for additional strikes
> be "unbalancing". You can Blur and blast away a .44 or Assault Rifle,
> and unlike the non-melee-weapon Chainsaw (with no modifiers appilicable
> to the strike whatsoever), you can use ammo cards for the guns.
> It's still an easy obstacle to deal with with a reasonable combat
> deck: manuevers or Shattering Blow.

I feel this would be very unbalancing:
a submachine gun also deals 3 damage, and costs 4 pool instead of 2.
Yes, it has a manouver, but if you use it, the only strike you may play
is a submachine one (sometimes I suddenly want to play a dodge or a
combat ends if things go wrong), and
yes, one could use ammo cards, but that ability shouldn't cost 2 extra pool.

Realisticly, I feel a chainsaw is far too heavy to use fast and often and
you cannot count chainsaw strikes, liek you can count sword strikes or
gun shots.

I'll go for the 'can only be used once per round' version (no melee).

Messages.Author: Kevin Lowe
Messages.Body:
GRACE WARD (war...@nevada.edu) wrote:
: PLEASE LISTEN

: SHOTGUN is to .44 as CHAINSAW is to BROADSWORD

: At least that's how it should have been

: Does anybody else out there see this relationship???

That is a good comparison, but remember that while the shotgun and .44
both cost 2 pool, as does the chainsaw, the sword only costs 1. If the
chainsaw only cost 1 pool no one could argue with you, but since it costs
two pool it should do more than it does. That's what this argument is
all about. (As I am far from the first to point out, the shotgun is in
every way better than the chainsaw... same cost, ranged damage, can use
ammo cards, no drawbacks. Since every other weapon has its use, this is
so odd it is almost certainly an error).

This argument is more or less moot anyway, until Dr Garfield or someone
at WOTC gives us the right version.

My two cents (using logic similar to above):
The costs for all the weapons are a little screwy, IMHO. The Ivory Bow
is too cheap, the Flame Thrower is too expensive vis a vis the 'Bow. The
.44 (2R damage) costs 2 pool, the Submachinegun (3R) 4 pool, the Assault
Rifle (4R) 5 pool. The Deer Rifle kind of sucks, too, but I don't see
what else it could cost :-).

I don't think we're ever going to get a universally acceptable rewrite
of the Chainsaw by extrapolating from the other weapons, or from the WOTC
clown show, or from Garfield. Let's use them for toilet paper as WOTC
intended and stop worrying about it.

(Possibly we could send it to Japan so they can use it as a Zen koan...
"If there is a correct text for the Chainsaw, but no one knows it, does
it truly exist? Speak!").

Yours, Kevin Lowe.

Messages.Author: L. Scott Johnson
Messages.Body:
Sorry if this gets posted twice:
I cancelled the original article due to a few math errors.
----------------------------------------------------------

kw...@cs.cornell.edu (Alan Kwan) writes:
[Ivory Bow is too cheap]

>Yes it is. 1 pool is simply deliberately the Mt$ $$$-man's game
>rare card idea. 1R aggravated is very powerful in the game.
>If it costs 2 pool and is not unique, no one (except $$$-poor
>players) will be using .44's!

The costs for weapons follows a simple formula (not that such a formula
was used):

Maybe my formula is unbalanced in favor of some aspects of game
play, or not (I haven't seen weapons abused too much) but it seems to lend
support to the statement "Maybe WotC attempted to balance the weapons
without regard to rarity".

Weapon Cost = F * ( damage - 1 )

F = 3/4 for normal weapons
F = 4/4 for Melee weapons
F = 5/4 for Ranged weapons
F = 6/4 for Guns (Ranged, ammo-using weapons)

treat aggravated damage as ( 2 * damage )
If (damage-1) is negative, use zero instead.

Note: the real formula shouldn't treat a 1-damage normal weapon the
same as a 1-damage gun, but my equation does (by multiplying by zero).

Combat Modifiers:
-----------------
+ 1 per maneuver
+ 1 if damage modifiers are also aggravated
- 0.5 if unique (not a combat effect, but rather: a generic effect).

Round fractions to nearset whole number.
(one .5 is rounded down, but this is necessary for the jump between
2 and 5 for .44 and Assault Rifle (2 and 4 damage, resp.). I suppose I
could've found an exponential (parabolic) curve to fit, but...)

NOTE: with this equation, being unique did not affect the rounded result
for any of the weapons.

Basic examples:
---------------
Bastard Sword: (1.00 * (2-1)) = 1 (= 1)
Sengir Dagger (1agg->2) (1.00 * (2-1) +1 -0.5) = 1.5 (= 2)
Ivory Bow (1agg->2) (1.25 * (2-1) -0.5) = 0.75 (= 1)
Flame Thrower (2agg->4) (1.25 * (4-1)) = 3.75 (= 4)
Saturday Night Special: (1.50 * (1-1) +1) = 1 (= 1)
Deer Rifle: (1.50 * (1-1) +1 +1) = 2 (= 2)
.44 Magnum: (1.50 * (2-1) +1) = 2.5 (? 2)
Submachine Gun: (1.50 * (3-1) +1) = 4 (= 4)
Assault Rifle: (1.50 * (4-1) +1) = 4.5 (= 5)

Special effects:
----------------
(These modifiers are chosen to fit a particular weapon)

If weilder can initiate Combat, use (2*damage) for damage. (Talbot's Chainsaw)

+1 per optional press. (Talbot's Chainsaw)
+2/S for paralyzation with S unmodified strikes. (Stake, Rowan Ring)
-1 if paralyzation transfers the weapon to the victim. (Stake, Rowan Ring)
-X if a weapon does X damage to its owner. (Grenade, Bomb)
-X/2 if a weapon deals X damage to friendly minions. (Talbot's Chainsaw)
+X if a weapon prevents X damage to its owner. (Talbot's Chainsaw)

Halve total cost for each of:
only use at long range. (RPG)
no use on first round of combat. (RPG)
only use once per combat. (Chainsaw, Shotgun, Grenade, Bomb)
use burns the weapon. (Grenade, Bomb)

Double total cost for each of:
can be eqipped during combat. (Zip Gun)

Modifiers for out of combat effects (after all combat costs are computed):
+1 Arson. (Bomb)
+0.5 per action-specific stealth. (Talbot's Chainsaw)
+1 per generic stealth. (?)
-1 if owner cannot hunt. (Talbot's Chainsaw)

Examples:
---------
Chainsaw: (0.75 * (3-1)) / 2 = 0.75 (= 1)
Talbot's Chainsaw: (0.75 * (6-1) +1 +1 -1.5 -0.5)
(Rush3->6) + 0.5 - 1 = 3.25 (= 3)
Stake: (1.00 * (1-1) +1 -1) = 0 (= 0)
Rowan Ring: (1.00 * ( 0 ) +2 -1 -0.5) = 0.5 (= 1)
Grenade: (1.25 * (3-1) -1) / 4 = 0.375 (= 0)
Bomb: (1.25 * (5-1) -5) / 4 +1 = 1 (= 1)
RPG Launcher: (1.25 * (6-1) / 4 = 1.563 (= 2)
Zip gun: (1.50 * (1-1) +1 -1) * 2 = 0 (= 0)
Shotgun: (1.50 * (3-1)) / 2 = 1.5 (= 2)

The only thing which comes out wrong is the chainsaw, but we all know that
no formula should have the chainsaw equivalent in cost to the Shotgun.

House Chainsaw:
Melee: (1.00 * (3-1)) / 2 = 1 (someone posted this)
Once per Round: (0.75 * (3-1)) = 1.5 (= 2)

(Actually, once per round should have some modifier as well, but...)

Messages.Author: Yousef G Master
Messages.Body:
I think you have to look at more than just math equations and what effect
the weapon has when played. For example, a .44 is not that deadly since
the average vamp does 1 damage already. If one of my vamps get's hit by
a .44, I think to myself, "boy that sucks." Even if they get additional
stikes, I feel bad, but not that bad. If I'm facing a submachine gun,
it's a completely different game. Even if I maneuver close to him, if
the combat continues past one round, I'm probably toast and I never did
any real damage to him. If he's got celerity, then I get REALLY
worried.

Some of the diplomacy factors are also important. Ie: what usually
happens in your games when someone pulls a ivory bow or sengir dagger?

I play with every type of weapon except the cainsaw. As for that I
clearly have to agree with the general sentiment. But for the rest of
the weapons, I think they're balanced.

-Yousef
